verdict.reasoning: Every factual assertion in the claim was independently verified against fresh 300dpi renders of both pages and against the raw transcription. PDF page 606 (printed folio 576), rendered via scripts/spec/page_workunit.py: the last printed body content is the Format 2 (temporal) general-format diagram -- 'ACCEPT identifier-2 FROM { DATE [YYYYMMDD] / DAY [YYYYDDD] / DAY-OF-WEEK / TIME } [ END-ACCEPT ]'. Below it is roughly a quarter page of whitespace, then the footer '576 (c)ISO/IEC 2023' and the license line. I see no 'Format 3' string anywhere on the page. Confirmed. PDF page 607 (printed folio 577): below the running header 'ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)', the FIRST body line is 'Format 3 (screen):', followed by 'ACCEPT screen-name-1' and the Format 3 diagram. Confirmed. Transcription, specs/ISO_COBOL.md: a whole-file grep for 'Format 3 \(screen\)' returns exactly ONE hit, line 25254, and that hit is the tail of the Format 2 display-math line -- the literal text is '...\text{ ]}$$ Format 3 (screen):' with no newline between the closing '$$' and the label. Line 25255 is blank and line 25256 is '', so the label sits inside the page-606 slice. The generated page-606 work unit ends at exactly that glued line, and the page-607 slice opens with the header then 'ACCEPT screen-name-1' (line 25261) with no format label preceding it. Every quotation in the claim is verbatim accurate; nothing is misquoted. I actively tried to dismiss this as page-break furniture and could not. Two independent defects survive: (1) Line-join defect: the label is concatenated onto the closing delimiter of a display-math block rather than standing as its own paragraph. This is not wrapping or hyphenation -- it is a block-boundary violation. A markdown+KaTeX renderer emits the Format 2 formula as a block and then trails 'Format 3 (screen):' against it, so the label visually captions the Format 2 diagram it does not belong to. Compare the correctly-formed sibling labels on the same page: 'Format 1 (device):' (line 25248) and 'Format 2 (temporal):' (line 25252) each occupy their own line with blank lines around them. The Format 3 label alone is malformed, which rules out a deliberate house style. (2) Page-attribution defect: this transcription's contract is per-page fidelity via '' anchors and '## Page NNN' headings, and the reconciliation tooling slices on exactly those anchors. Under that contract the label is in the wrong slice, and the page-607 slice delivers an unlabeled general format. One honest qualification, which is why I amended the description: in LINEAR reading order the transcription is NOT wrong. The label still precedes the Format 3 syntax, so a reader consuming the file top-to-bottom is not misled about which format is which, and no text is lost, dropped, or altered. The claim's framing that 'anyone reading page 606 sees a stray label attached to the wrong figure' overstates the semantic harm -- the harm is rendering and page attribution, not COBOL meaning. No syntax element, choice indicator, bracket, brace, or underline is affected. Severity is correctly 'structural' rather than semantic.
verdict.corrected_description: CONFIRMED, with the harm narrowed. The transcription omits the required line break between the Format 2 display-math block and the 'Format 3 (screen):' label: specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 25254 ends '...\text{ ]}$$ Format 3 (screen):', concatenating the label onto the closing '$$'. Because that line falls before the '' anchor on line 25256, the label also lands in the page-606 slice, whereas the PDF prints it as the first body line of page 607 (folio 577) above 'ACCEPT screen-name-1'; PDF page 606 (folio 576) genuinely ends with the Format 2 diagram, whitespace, and the footer. The label is the only one of the three format labels in 14.9.1.2 that is malformed -- 'Format 1 (device):' (line 25248) and 'Format 2 (temporal):' (line 25252) are each correctly on their own line. Two consequences, both verified: the label renders as trailing text captioning the Format 2 formula rather than as a heading for Format 3, and the page-607 slice presents 'ACCEPT screen-name-1' plus its diagram with no format label at all. Scope correction to the original claim: no text is lost and linear reading order is preserved -- the label still precedes the Format 3 syntax in document order, so a top-to-bottom reader is not misled about which format is which, and no syntax element, bracket, brace, choice indicator, or underline is affected. The defect is presentational and page-attribution only. Fix: split line 25254 so the label begins a new paragraph, and move it below the '' anchor to match the PDF's page assignment.
